source.original:
"On the top floor, there are two
rooms.

First, the room on the left.
It’s the Union Room.

You may link up with Trainers
around you who have also entered\lthe Union Room.

With them, you may do things like
chat, battle, and trade.

Second, the room on the right is
the DIRECT CORNER.

You may trade or battle Pokémon
with your friends in this room.

If the Wireless Adapter isn’t
connected, you may still link up\lusing a GBA Game Link cable.

If that is the case, you must go
to the Direct Corner.

I hope you enjoy the Wireless 
Communication System."

source.original:
"Let me explain how the Pokémon
Wireless Club works.

On this, the top floor, there are
two rooms.

First, the room on the left.
It’s the Union Room.

You may link up with Trainers
around you who have also entered\lthe Union Room.

With them, you may do things like
chat, battle, and trade.

Second, the room on the right is
the Direct Corner.

You may trade or battle Pokémon
with your friends in this room.

Sometimes, you may not be able to
find your friends in the Union Room\lor the Direct Corner.

In that case, please move closer
to your friends.

If the Wireless Adapter isn’t
connected, you may still link up\lusing a GBA Game Link cable.

If that is the case, you must go
to the Direct Corner.

I hope you enjoy the Wireless 
Communication System."
source.translation_source: Let me explain how the Pokémon Wireless Club works. On this, the top floor, there are two rooms. First, the room on the left. It’s the Union Room. You may link up with Trainers around you who have also entered the Union Room. With them, you may do things like chat, battle, and trade. Second, the room on the right is the Direct Corner. You may trade or battle Pokémon with your friends in this room. Sometimes, you may not be able to find your friends in the Union Room or the Direct Corner. In that case, please move closer to your friends. If the Wireless Adapter isn’t connected, you may still link up using a GBA Game Link cable. If that is the case, you must go to the Direct Corner. I hope you enjoy the Wireless Communication System.

tell you about how you can battle\lPokémon!

person and for sure!

All righty, here goes!

Keep your eyes glued to the super
POKé DUDE SHOW!"

source.original:
"Today, the POKé DUDE’s here to
tell you about status problems!

Status problems include poisoning,
paralysis, sleep, burn\.

There are a couple others, but
they really are trouble.

Get any one, and your Pokémon
may become useless in battle.

You know, it hurts the POKé DUDE
to see a Pokémon suffer\.

So, what should you do if your
Pokémon gets a status problem?

Well, you’ve got me to show you!

All righty, here goes!

Keep your eyes glued to the super
POKé DUDE SHOW!"

source.original:
"Does everyone know about type
matchups?

Pokémon and their moves all
belong to certain types.

For example, there are such types
as GRASS and WATER.

You need to consider the type of
the move used to attack\.

And, the type of the Pokémon that
is hit by that attack.

Depending on how those two types
match up, the damage can change.

You see, it depends on whether
the type matchup is good or bad.

If you don’t know how matchups
work, battles will be tough.

So, let me demonstrate exactly
what I mean.

All righty, here goes!

Keep your eyes glued to the super
POKé DUDE SHOW!"

source.original:
"Thirty years ago, a large meteorite
was hurtling towards Borrius.

The astronomers in Seaport City
predicted that if it wasn’t\lstopped, it would fall directly on\lValley City, this city, and end all\llife living here.

With great haste, we began our
evacuation of the city.

As we were about to make our escape
through the SES Expressway, we\lheard the news.

The meteorite was now predicted to
crush half of the region!

If we attempted to flee
underground, there would be a\llarge chance we’d be buried alive.

Chaos ensued.

All was thought hopeless\.until
HE arrived.

[green]Aros[blue], the legend.

He arrived alongside Arceus
and used a small Pokémon to\lteleport everyone to East Borrius,\lsafe from harm.

He planned to attack the meteorite
head on and smash it to bits.

Once he had transported everyone to
safety, it is said that he rode on\la Rayquaza and smashed into\lthe meteorite!

It shattered, and most of the
smaller fragments fell on\lValley City.

The city was destroyed, but Aros
had saved a region.

I will never forget the heroic act
that man performed."
source.translation_source: Thirty years ago, a large meteorite was hurtling towards Borrius. The astronomers in Seaport City predicted that if it wasn’t stopped, it would fall directly on Valley City, this city, and end all life living here. With great haste, we began our evacuation of the city. As we were about to make our escape through the SES Expressway, we heard the news. The meteorite was now predicted to crush half of the region! If we attempted to flee underground, there would be a large chance we’d be buried alive. Chaos ensued. All was thought hopeless[game-token-1]until HE arrived. [color-green-2]Aros[color-blue-3], the legend. He arrived alongside Arceus and used a small Pokémon to teleport everyone to East Borrius, safe from harm. He planned to attack the meteorite head on and smash it to bits. Once he had transported everyone to safety, it is said that he rode on a Rayquaza and smashed into the meteorite! It shattered, and most of the smaller fragments fell on Valley City. The city was destroyed, but Aros had saved a region. I will never forget the heroic act that man performed.

source.original:
"The Mega Ring lets you use the
power of Mega Evolution.

To access it, the Pokémon battling
must be holding its Mega Stone.

To Mega Evolve in battle, when you
see the Mega symbol appear, press\lthe Start Button.

Your Pokémon will then Mega Evolve
and become even more powerful!

Just remember, you can only Mega
Evolve one Pokémon per battle.

The Mega Evolution’s effects will
wear off once the battle is over,\lso choose carefully.

I have faith that you’ll use this
Mega Ring to help benefit humanity.

Don’t let me down, [player].

I’m counting on you to make a
difference in the world."

I have faith that you’ll use this Mega Ring to help benefit humanity. Don’t let me down, [player-name-1]. I’m counting on you to make a difference in the world.

source.original:
"A Mission is an extra objective you
receive by accepting a request for\lhelp.

Many people out there are unable to
solve their own problems and\lrequire assistance from others.

Once you accept the Mission, the
details are automatically recorded\lin the Quest Log.

Missions can often yield great
rewards, be it items, money, or\leven new areas to explore.

If someone requests a Mission from
you, accept it immediately.

Even if you have no intention of
completing it right away, there’s\lno harm in having it registered in\lyour Quest Log.

With that being said, there are
several people here in need of\lassistance.

Look around and see if there’s
anyone you’d like to help!

And come see me when you’ve
completed at least [green]5[blue] Missions."
source.translation_source: A Mission is an extra objective you receive by accepting a request for help. Many people out there are unable to solve their own problems and require assistance from others. Once you accept the Mission, the details are automatically recorded in the Quest Log. Missions can often yield great rewards, be it items, money, or even new areas to explore. If someone requests a Mission from you, accept it immediately. Even if you have no intention of completing it right away, there’s no harm in having it registered in your Quest Log. With that being said, there are several people here in need of assistance. Look around and see if there’s anyone you’d like to help! And come see me when you’ve completed at least [color-green-1]5[color-blue-2] Missions.

most lowlives in the region are\ldrawn here, causing crime rates to\ldecrease everywhere else.

didn’t fight back after they were\lforcibly expelled during the riots.

They won’t tell you that, though.

In order for Antisis City to keep
on existing as is, the police need\lto feign ignorance to anything\lthat’s not too serious of a crime.

But if anything starts to get out
of hand around here, that’s when\lBig Mo comes in and takes control."

But if anything starts to get out of hand around here, that’s when Big Mo comes in and takes control.

source.original:
"In the [green]Classic Leaders Gauntlet[blue],
you’ll be pitted against each Gym\lLeader, one after the other.

But despite the fights being back
to back, you will get a chance to\lsave and adjust your team in\lbetween each fight.

As for the Gym Leaders’ teams,
they’ll be using much stronger\lPokémon than when you fought\lthem in their Gyms.

They’ll also be fighting with the
same battle effects as back then,\lso keep that in mind.

If you manage to defeat a Gym
Leader, and you’ve already\lreceived a Z-Crystal from them,\lthey’ll give you their daily Gem\lafter the battle, assuming they\lhaven’t already given you one.

If you manage to defeat
all of them, you’ll win fantastic\lprizes!

And of course, the harder your
[green]Battle Difficulty[blue], the better the\lprizes you can win."
source.translation_source: In the [color-green-1]Classic Leaders Gauntlet[color-blue-2], you’ll be pitted against each Gym Leader, one after the other. But despite the fights being back to back, you will get a chance to save and adjust your team in between each fight. As for the Gym Leaders’ teams, they’ll be using much stronger Pokémon than when you fought them in their Gyms. They’ll also be fighting with the same battle effects as back then, so keep that in mind. If you manage to defeat a Gym Leader, and you’ve already received a Z-Crystal from them, they’ll give you their daily Gem after the battle, assuming they haven’t already given you one. If you manage to defeat all of them, you’ll win fantastic prizes! And of course, the harder your [color-green-3]Battle Difficulty[color-blue-4], the better the prizes you can win.

ages, I say, since I’ve felt such a\lstrong urge to cross paths with a\lfellow Trainer once more.

Hello again, and my heartiest
congratulations on becoming\lChampion.

And, I suppose, my most heartfelt
thanks for ridding the world of a\lmost terrible evil.

I remember when we last battled, I
was fortunate enough to catch you\lquite near the end of your quest\lto the Pokémon League.

You were much like a Butterfree,
newly emerged, with nothing left\lbut to wait for its wings to dry\land harden.

But now, I wish to see your
strength at its fullest.

What did you experience?

What ground have you tread as you
lived through those moments?

I desire another battle, so I may
observe the results.

Will you indulge this old man?"

"The DexNav consists of two parts:
an [green]interface[blue] and a [green]search bar[blue].

The interface can be accessed from
the [green]Start Menu[blue] and allows you to\lchoose a Pokémon to search for.

If a Pokémon can be found in your
current location, and the Pokémon\lis registered as at least \qo[green]seen[blue]\qc\lin your Pokédex, then it will\lappear as searchable.

Once a Pokémon is chosen with \btn00,
it will appear on the search bar\lwhile the search is active.

To find the Pokémon you’ve chosen
to search for, keep an eye out for\lphenomenon such as [green]rustling grass[blue]\lor [green]dust clouds[blue] in caves.

You need to approach these slowly,
otherwise the Pokémon will flee.

Do note that if the Pokémon is
not registered as \qo[green]caught[blue]\qc in your\lPokédex, it may be difficult to\llocate before it is captured.

Each time you encounter a Pokémon
with the DexNav, its [green]search level[blue]\lincreases, and future searches may\lyield better Pokémon."
source.translation_source: The DexNav consists of two parts: an [color-green-1]interface[color-blue-2] and a [color-green-3]search bar[color-blue-4]. The interface can be accessed from the [color-green-5]Start Menu[color-blue-6] and allows you to choose a Pokémon to search for. If a Pokémon can be found in your current location, and the Pokémon is registered as at least [quote-open-7][color-green-8]seen[color-blue-9][quote-close-10] in your Pokédex, then it will appear as searchable. Once a Pokémon is chosen with [button-icon-11], it will appear on the search bar while the search is active. To find the Pokémon you’ve chosen to search for, keep an eye out for phenomenon such as [color-green-12]rustling grass[color-blue-13] or [color-green-14]dust clouds[color-blue-15] in caves. You need to approach these slowly, otherwise the Pokémon will flee. Do note that if the Pokémon is not registered as [quote-open-16][color-green-17]caught[color-blue-18][quote-close-19] in your Pokédex, it may be difficult to locate before it is captured. Each time you encounter a Pokémon with the DexNav, its [color-green-20]search level[color-blue-21] increases, and future searches may yield better Pokémon.

source.original:
"When searching for Pokémon, you
can choose to search for either\lland-based Pokémon or water-based\lPokémon.

Water-based Pokémon include both
Pokémon found by Surfing and by\lFishing.

However, Pokémon found by fishing
will only appear as searchable if\lyou have obtained the necessary\lRod to hook them yourself.

Additionally, it is important to
note, regardless of the Pokémon\lyou are searching for, it will be\lmuch more difficult to find if\lyou have not caught the species\lprior."
source.translation_source: When searching for Pokémon, you can choose to search for either land-based Pokémon or water-based Pokémon. Water-based Pokémon include both Pokémon found by Surfing and by Fishing. However, Pokémon found by fishing will only appear as searchable if you have obtained the necessary Rod to hook them yourself. Additionally, it is important to note, regardless of the Pokémon you are searching for, it will be much more difficult to find if you have not caught the species prior.

source.original:
"Chaining is when the DexNav is
used to encounter Pokémon many\ltimes in a row.

A chain builds every time you
capture or defeat a Pokémon\lencountered with the DexNav.

If you do not capture or defeat the
Pokémon, the chain breaks.

A chain will also break if, outside
of battle, a Pokémon runs away\lfrom you or you encounter a\lPokémon not using the DexNav.

Saving and restarting the game
also breaks the chain.

The chain resets every 100 battles,
and the higher the chain, the\lhigher the Pokémon level.

Additionally, whenever the chain
reaches 50 or 100, Pokémon have a\lhigher chance of being found shiny.

This is indicated by a gold star next
to the chain length on the HUD."
source.translation_source: Chaining is when the DexNav is used to encounter Pokémon many times in a row. A chain builds every time you capture or defeat a Pokémon encountered with the DexNav. If you do not capture or defeat the Pokémon, the chain breaks. A chain will also break if, outside of battle, a Pokémon runs away from you or you encounter a Pokémon not using the DexNav. Saving and restarting the game also breaks the chain. The chain resets every 100 battles, and the higher the chain, the higher the Pokémon level. Additionally, whenever the chain reaches 50 or 100, Pokémon have a higher chance of being found shiny. This is indicated by a gold star next to the chain length on the HUD.

source.original:
"Twenty years ago, a large meteorite
was hurtling towards Borrius.

The astronomers at Cube Corp.
predicted that if it wasn’t\lstopped, it would fall directly on\lValley City, this city, and end all\llife living here.

With great haste, we began our
evacuation of the city.

As we were about to make our escape
through the KBT Expressway, we\lheard the news.

The meteorite was now predicted to
crush half of the region!

If we attempted to flee
underground, there would be a\llarge chance we’d be buried alive.

Chaos ensued.

All was thought hopeless\. until
HE arrived.

[green]Aros[blue], the legend.

He arrived alongside a small Pokémon
he used to teleport everyone to\lEast Borrius, safe from harm.

He planned to attack the meteorite
head on and smash it to bits.

Once he had transported everyone to
safety, it is said that he rode on\la Rayquaza and smashed into\lthe meteorite!

It shattered, and most of the
smaller fragments fell on\lValley City.

The city was destroyed, but Aros
had saved a region.

I will never forget the heroic act
that man performed."
source.translation_source: Twenty years ago, a large meteorite was hurtling towards Borrius. The astronomers at Cube Corp. predicted that if it wasn’t stopped, it would fall directly on Valley City, this city, and end all life living here. With great haste, we began our evacuation of the city. As we were about to make our escape through the KBT Expressway, we heard the news. The meteorite was now predicted to crush half of the region! If we attempted to flee underground, there would be a large chance we’d be buried alive. Chaos ensued. All was thought hopeless[game-token-1] until HE arrived. [color-green-2]Aros[color-blue-3], the legend. He arrived alongside a small Pokémon he used to teleport everyone to East Borrius, safe from harm. He planned to attack the meteorite head on and smash it to bits. Once he had transported everyone to safety, it is said that he rode on a Rayquaza and smashed into the meteorite! It shattered, and most of the smaller fragments fell on Valley City. The city was destroyed, but Aros had saved a region. I will never forget the heroic act that man performed.

source.original:
"Following the meteorite strike all
those years ago, two Pokémon were\ldiscovered to have landed on Earth.

One of them was a very powerful
Pokémon capable of granting any\lwish the heart desired.

At first, the townspeople and I
thought this was wonderful!

We could use it to restore our
broken city!

However, we soon learned that all
our wishes came at a cost.

Fearing an even more devastating
outcome, we locked up this Pokémon.

But now that the [buffer2] of Aros
has become Champion, I feel that it\lis fitting we bestow this Pokémon\lunto you.

Would you care to give this
Pokémon a loving home?"
source.translation_source: Following the meteorite strike all those years ago, two Pokémon were discovered to have landed on Earth. One of them was a very powerful Pokémon capable of granting any wish the heart desired. At first, the townspeople and I thought this was wonderful! We could use it to restore our broken city! However, we soon learned that all our wishes came at a cost. Fearing an even more devastating outcome, we locked up this Pokémon. But now that the [buffer2-1] of Aros has become Champion, I feel that it is fitting we bestow this Pokémon unto you. Would you care to give this Pokémon a loving home?

\.

using it\. hmm, yes."

source.original:
"Let me tell ya something, young
feller.

To the east of here is a
vast desert.

It is so amazing, that it is
simply called the [green]Great Desert[blue].

Words can’t even begin to
describe it!

However, it’s really difficult to
traverse without the proper gear.

So don’t think ya can just waltz
out there without preppin’ first.

Yer outfit seems a little hot
for the desert, but it’ll do ya a\lgood job of protecting yer body.

As for yer eyes, I’d recommend
getting yerself a good pair of\l[green]Go-Goggles[blue].

In fact, I’d actually be willing to
give ya mine if ya can show me how\lstrong ya are by [green]beatin’ the Gym[blue]."

Yer outfit seems a little hot for the desert, but it’ll do ya a good job of protecting yer body. As for yer eyes, I’d recommend getting yerself a good pair of [color-green-3]Go-Goggles[color-blue-4]. In fact, I’d actually be willing to give ya mine if ya can show me how strong ya are by [color-green-5]beatin’ the Gym[color-blue-6].

source.original:
"Can you read?
Not everyone can.

I can’t, and I failed the first
grade a couple of times now.

Can you show me the awesome power
of basic literacy?

Trainer Tips signs should be good
examples for words and such."

source.original:
"A Gem is a special type of held
item that powers up a single attack\lin battle.

Each Gem corresponds to a specific
Type and can only power up that\lType of move.

Gems usually disappear after use,
but like most consumable items,\lthey’re returned to you after\limportant battles, such as battles\lagainst Gym Leaders.

Most Gym Leaders in Borrius have at
least one of their Pokémon holding\la Gem, so be wary.

If you’re concerned about this, you
can use the move [green]Incinerate[blue] to\lmelt their Gem first, before they\lhave a chance to use it."
source.translation_source: A Gem is a special type of held item that powers up a single attack in battle. Each Gem corresponds to a specific Type and can only power up that Type of move. Gems usually disappear after use, but like most consumable items, they’re returned to you after important battles, such as battles against Gym Leaders. Most Gym Leaders in Borrius have at least one of their Pokémon holding a Gem, so be wary. If you’re concerned about this, you can use the move [color-green-1]Incinerate[color-blue-2] to melt their Gem first, before they have a chance to use it.

source.original:
"A Mission is an extra objective you
receive by accepting a request\lfor help.

Many people out there are unable to
solve their own problems and\lrequire assistance from others.

Once you accept the Mission, the
details are automatically recorded\lin the Mission Log.

Missions can often yield great
rewards, be it items, money, or\leven new areas to explore.

If someone requests a Mission from
you, accept it immediately.

Even if you have no intention of
completing it right away, there’s\lno harm in having it registered\lin your Mission Log.

With that being said, there are
several people here in need\lof assistance.

Look around and see if there’s
anyone you’d like to help!

And come see me when you’ve
completed at least [green]5[blue] Missions."

Many people out there are unable to solve their own problems and require assistance from others. Once you accept the Mission, the details are automatically recorded in the Mission Log. Look around and see if there’s anyone you’d like to help! And come see me when you’ve completed at least [color-green-1]5[color-blue-2] Missions.

"I’m sure you already know, but with
that [green]Mission Log[red] device your mother\lgave you, you can record various\lrequests from people.

Some of these people may ask you
to complete a certain task some\lfinite number of times.

It may seem daunting at first, but
these people really just want to\lknow if you have satisfied their\lrequest at some point in your\ljourney.

So go on, keep exploring!

You’ll be amazed to see what kind
of things you can accomplish while\ltravelling.

In fact, sometimes they will even
make requests for things you have\lalready done!

In that case, you may ask them for
a reward right away.

Good luck on your journey!"

source.original:
"New Game \+ is a special feature that
allows you to start a new game\lwith special bonuses:

1) A team of max 6 Pokémon can
be carried over to the new game.

These 6 Pokémon are created from
the party in the previous save.

The Pokémon will be devolved to
their base species and will forget\lany moves barring Egg Moves.

Held items will be retained barring
Z-Crystals.

Additionally, stats such as EVs and
IVs will be retained.

2) If any of the following items
have been obtained in the previous\lsave, they will be carried over to\lthe new game:

Stat Scanner, Motorcycle, DexNav,
Dowsing Machine, Baby Monitor, ADM,\lTrainer Catalogue, Shiny Charm,\lOval Charm, Catching Charm, Magma\lStone, Frontier Card, Porta-PC,\lTime Turner, any unlocked item\lupgrades, and any BP earned.

3) The game’s difficulty may be
increased or decreased at any point\lwithout penalty.

4) Certain main story puzzles
solved in the previous save will\lremain solved in the new game.

5) If the Frontier Card is carried
over, then the Battle Frontier\lmay be accessed immediately upon\larrival in Seaport City.

6) Additional NPCs for modifying
IVs, EVs, and natures will be\lavailable in Crater Town until\lthe game is cleared (when not\lplaying on Sandbox Mode).

Note that some may charge BP for
their services, so make sure you\learn enough before starting the\lnew game.

7) Certain Legendary Pokémon
previously locked to the post-game\lwill now be obtainable before the\lgame is cleared."

These 6 Pokémon are created from the party in the previous save. The Pokémon will be devolved to their base species and will forget any moves barring Egg Moves. Held items will be retained barring Z-Crystals. Additionally, stats such as EVs and IVs will be retained. 2) If any of the following items have been obtained in the previous save, they will be carried over to the new game: Stat Scanner, Motorcycle, DexNav, Dowsing Machine, Baby Monitor, ADM, Trainer Catalogue, Shiny Charm, Oval Charm, Catching Charm, Magma Stone, Frontier Card, Porta-PC, Time Turner, any unlocked item upgrades, and any BP earned. 3) The game’s difficulty may be increased or decreased at any point without penalty. 4) Certain main story puzzles solved in the previous save will remain solved in the new game. 5) If the Frontier Card is carried over, then the Battle Frontier may be accessed immediately upon arrival in Seaport City. 6) Additional NPCs for modifying IVs, EVs, and natures will be available in Crater Town until the game is cleared (when not playing on Sandbox Mode). Note that some may charge BP for their services, so make sure you earn enough before starting the new game. 7) Certain Legendary Pokémon previously locked to the post-game will now be obtainable before the game is cleared.

source.original:
"The rules are simple.

Choose one Pokémon to battle three
Trainers in a row.

Each Trainer is also only using
one Pokémon.

You can use whatever Pokémon you
want in the ring, but you can’t use\l[green]Flying[blue]-, [green]Psychic[blue]-, or [green]Fairy[blue]-type\lmoves in the battles.

For moves that change their types
in battles, we only care about the\ltypes those moves become.

We don’t like those types here in
the ring, and Big Mo won’t let you\luse the [green]most common of those move\lon your team[blue] if you get to him.

If some types appear equally on
your team, we’ll ban the types in\lthe order of Flying, Psychic, and\lthen Fairy.

So, say you have a Toucannon and an
Alakazam on your team, you won’t\lbe able to use Flying-type moves\lagainst Big Mo, since Flying comes\lbefore Psychic.

Got it?

Don’t get confused!"

You can use whatever Pokémon you want in the ring, but you can’t use [color-green-1]Flying[color-blue-2]-, [color-green-3]Psychic[color-blue-4]-, or [color-green-5]Fairy[color-blue-6]-type moves in the battles. For moves that change their types in battles, we only care about the types those moves become. We don’t like those types here in the ring, and Big Mo won’t let you use the [color-green-7]most common of those move on your team[color-blue-8] if you get to him. If some types appear equally on your team, we’ll ban the types in the order of Flying, Psychic, and then Fairy. So, say you have a Toucannon and an Alakazam on your team, you won’t be able to use Flying-type moves against Big Mo, since Flying comes before Psychic. Got it? Don’t get confused!

source.original:
"As you can or can’t see, this Gym
is centred around [green]Dark[blue]-types.

If you want to win here, a good
starting point would be bringing\l[green]Fighting[blue]-, [green]Bug[blue]- or [green]Fairy[blue]-types.

Just be aware, because of the many
Trainers that struggle in this Gym,\l[green]negative emotions[blue] will fill the air\las you battle.

These emotions will inflict damage
at the end of each turn.

Only [green]Dark[blue]-types, [green]Psychic[blue]-types,
[green]Ghost[blue]-types, and Pokémon with the\lAbilities [green]Magic Guard[blue], [green]Unaware[blue], or\l[green]Oblivious[blue] are unaffected.

If you end up struggling because of
the negative emotions, bringing a\lPokémon that isn’t affected could\lreally help you out.

Now, getting to Véga, the Leader,
is relatively simple.

Navigate the dimly lit hallways, and
don’t get spotted.

If you get spotted, you’ll either
have to battle some Trainers or be\lsent back to the beginning of\lthe hallway.

Every Trainer you defeat will
brighten up the room, so I\lrecommend battling them all first.

Good luck out there!"
source.translation_source: As you can or can’t see, this Gym is centred around [color-green-1]Dark[color-blue-2]-types. If you want to win here, a good starting point would be bringing [color-green-3]Fighting[color-blue-4]-, [color-green-5]Bug[color-blue-6]- or [color-green-7]Fairy[color-blue-8]-types. Just be aware, because of the many Trainers that struggle in this Gym, [color-green-9]negative emotions[color-blue-10] will fill the air as you battle. These emotions will inflict damage at the end of each turn. Only [color-green-11]Dark[color-blue-12]-types, [color-green-13]Psychic[color-blue-14]-types, [color-green-15]Ghost[color-blue-16]-types, and Pokémon with the Abilities [color-green-17]Magic Guard[color-blue-18], [color-green-19]Unaware[color-blue-20], or [color-green-21]Oblivious[color-blue-22] are unaffected. If you end up struggling because of the negative emotions, bringing a Pokémon that isn’t affected could really help you out. Now, getting to Véga, the Leader, is relatively simple. Navigate the dimly lit hallways, and don’t get spotted. If you get spotted, you’ll either have to battle some Trainers or be sent back to the beginning of the hallway. Every Trainer you defeat will brighten up the room, so I recommend battling them all first. Good luck out there!

source.original:
"Contrary to popular belief, this
Gym is not an Ice-type gym.

It’s a [green]Flying[blue]-type Gym!

And the best way to counter
Flying-types is to clip their\lwings with [green]ice[blue], [green]rocks[blue],\lor [green]electricity[blue]!

But be careful, because there’s a
tailwind in this Gym!

This [green]Tailwind[blue] will increase the
speed of all Flying-type Pokémon,\lso don’t get cocky just because\lyour Pokémon might have a high\lspeed stat.

Unless it’s part Flying-type,
of course.

Getting to Alice requires using
the fans and holes on the ground\lto move between levels of the Gym.

It’s not too complicated, just make
sure you remember where you have\land haven’t been before.

Good luck out there!"
source.translation_source: Contrary to popular belief, this Gym is not an Ice-type gym. It’s a [color-green-1]Flying[color-blue-2]-type Gym! And the best way to counter Flying-types is to clip their wings with [color-green-3]ice[color-blue-4], [color-green-5]rocks[color-blue-6], or [color-green-7]electricity[color-blue-8]! But be careful, because there’s a tailwind in this Gym! This [color-green-9]Tailwind[color-blue-10] will increase the speed of all Flying-type Pokémon, so don’t get cocky just because your Pokémon might have a high speed stat. Unless it’s part Flying-type, of course. Getting to Alice requires using the fans and holes on the ground to move between levels of the Gym. It’s not too complicated, just make sure you remember where you have and haven’t been before. Good luck out there!

\.

source.original:
"Have you ever heard of the curious
case of Benjamin Butterfree?

Born a Butterfree, fainted a
Caterpie, poor Benjamin aged\lbackwards his entire life.

And in the spirit of Butterfree,
our Leader, Benjamin designed\lthis Gym.

And you guessed it, in this Gym
Trainers like to use [green]Bug[blue]-types!

Bringing some [green]Rock[blue]-, [green]Flying[blue]-, or
[green]Fire[blue]-types can really put them\lin their place.

But be careful, because in this Gym
when a Pokémon is defeated, it\lregresses to an earlier state.

Pokémon only faint when they can
regress no more.

Because of this unique battling
condition, Pokémon won’t earn any\lExp. in this Gym.

And as for how to find Benjamin,
I’ll tell you this.

In each of the rooms along the
wall, buttons are hidden in rocks.

Press these buttons in the right
order, and you’ll open up a path\lto ol’ Benjamin.

can grow in more ways that just by\lleveling up?

your team will gain hidden stats\lcorresponding to the Pokémon you\ldefeated.

by using vitamins like Protein.

In fact, Prof. Log and I developed
a device capable of viewing these\lhidden stats, but a [green]vanilla[blue] Trainer\llike you shouldn’t worry about them\lat all.

So just go out and enjoy using
whatever you catch!"

source.original:
"You see\.

I have spent many years of my life
scouring the world in search of\lthe many different Vivillon.

Vivillon is a special Pokémon -
it has many different appearances.

Meadow, Archipelago, Continental,
Elegant, Garden, High Plains, Icy\lSnow, Jungle, Marine, Modern,\lMonsoon, Ocean, Polar, River,\lSandstorm, Savanna, Sun, Tundra,\lFancy, and one final special one.

And after many years, I have
succeeded in finding them all.

Of these 20 forms, I have hidden 19
of them around Borrius.

Do you think you’re up to the
challenge of hunting my Vivillon?

You do not need to capture them,
although, if you’re a collector\llike myself, you may wish to."

"Heya!

introduced myself.

My name’s Catherine!
But most people call me Cathy.

I came here from Kanto with my
friend Mahina.

Prof. Oak wanted us to complete the
Pokédex, so every day we travel\laround Borrius searching for as\lmany rare Pokémon as we can.

It’s thanks to these travels that I

source.original:
"Let me explain how the Pokémon
Wireless Club works.

On this, the top floor, there are
two rooms.

First, the room on the left.
It’s the Union Room.

You may link up with Trainers
around you who have also\lentered the Union Room using\lthe Wireless Adapter.

With them, you may do things like
chat, battle, and trade.

Second, the room on the right is
the Direct Corner.

You may battle Pokémon with your
friends in this room, but trading is\lno longer available.

Please use Unbound Cloud if you
wish to trade Pokémon.

Sometimes, you may not be able to
find your friends in the Union Room\lor the Direct Corner.

In that case, please move closer
to your friends.

If the Wireless Adapter isn’t
connected, you may still link up\lusing a GBA Game Link cable.

If that is the case, you must go
to the Direct Corner.

I hope you enjoy the Wireless
Communication System."
source.translation_source: Let me explain how the Pokémon Wireless Club works. On this, the top floor, there are two rooms. First, the room on the left. It’s the Union Room. You may link up with Trainers around you who have also entered the Union Room using the Wireless Adapter. With them, you may do things like chat, battle, and trade. Second, the room on the right is the Direct Corner. You may battle Pokémon with your friends in this room, but trading is no longer available. Please use Unbound Cloud if you wish to trade Pokémon. Sometimes, you may not be able to find your friends in the Union Room or the Direct Corner. In that case, please move closer to your friends. If the Wireless Adapter isn’t connected, you may still link up using a GBA Game Link cable. If that is the case, you must go to the Direct Corner. I hope you enjoy the Wireless Communication System.

source.original:
"Each member of the Elite Four likes
to set up certain conditions on the\lfield before battle.

First, there’s [green]Moleman[blue].

He likes to set up a vicious
Sandstorm, a kind of Sandstorm\lthat does more damage than a\lregular Sandstorm.

This kind of Sandstorm also boosts
Ground-type Pokémon’s Sp. Def,\land won’t go away if you try to\lget rid of it.

Next, there’s [green]Elias[blue].

source.original:
"Hey, Trainer!

Remember me?
I certainly remember you.

I’m the guy you met in Gurun Town!

My hope was to strike it big here
in East Borrius, but the only gig\lI could find involves fishing\.

Anyway, I was hired as a sporting
goods promoter by Cube Corp.

They wanted me to encourage
Trainers to fish more, and\lthereby promote their signature\lfishing rod band.

So, here’s my encouragement
to you!

If you fish for at least [green][buffer1][blue]
Pokémon using fishing rods you\lobtain yourself, you’ll be eligible\lfor a reward!

How does that sound?
Great, right?

Come back to me if you’ve fished at
least [green][buffer1][blue] times!"

My hope was to strike it big here in East Borrius, but the only gig I could find involves fishing[game-token-1] Anyway, I was hired as a sporting goods promoter by Cube Corp. They wanted me to encourage Trainers to fish more, and thereby promote their signature fishing rod band. So, here’s my encouragement to you! If you fish for at least [color-green-2][buffer1-3][color-blue-4] Pokémon using fishing rods you obtain yourself, you’ll be eligible for a reward! How does that sound? Great, right? Come back to me if you’ve fished at least [color-green-5][buffer1-6][color-blue-7] times!

source.original:
"This hole you see here is what’s
known as a Raid Den.

Powerful Pokémon inhabit these
dens, and once a day, you can fight\lfor a chance to capture one in\leach den found around Borrius!

These Pokémon are scary strong, so
it’s a good idea to pick the right\lpartner to fight alongside you.

When you start the battle, you’ll
notice that the Pokémon you’re\lfighting looks very big.

This is because of the phenomenon
known as [green]Dynamax[red].

It will stay this way throughout
the battle and can only be caught\lonce it is defeated and returned to\lnormal size."
source.translation_source: This hole you see here is what’s known as a Raid Den. Powerful Pokémon inhabit these dens, and once a day, you can fight for a chance to capture one in each den found around Borrius! These Pokémon are scary strong, so it’s a good idea to pick the right partner to fight alongside you. When you start the battle, you’ll notice that the Pokémon you’re fighting looks very big. This is because of the phenomenon known as [color-green-1]Dynamax[color-red-2]. It will stay this way throughout the battle and can only be caught once it is defeated and returned to normal size.

source.original:
"Dynamax is a unique phenomenon
that can only be used in special\lareas, like this one.

If you have mastered the power of
Mega Evolution, you’ll be able to\lDynamax your Pokémon as well.

Almost any Pokémon can Dynamax,
but if a Pokémon holds a Mega\lStone or Z-Crystal, it won’t be\lable to.

To Dynamax a Pokémon, press \btn04
when you see the red Dynamax\lsymbol appear.

If you choose to Dynamax your
Pokémon, the effect will last\lfor three turns.

During this time period, each of
your Pokémon’s moves will be\lpowered up into special variants\lknown as [green]Max Moves[red].

These Max Moves are much more
powerful than regular attacks,\lso make sure you use them to full\leffect while Dynamaxed!"
source.translation_source: Dynamax is a unique phenomenon that can only be used in special areas, like this one. If you have mastered the power of Mega Evolution, you’ll be able to Dynamax your Pokémon as well. Almost any Pokémon can Dynamax, but if a Pokémon holds a Mega Stone or Z-Crystal, it won’t be able to. To Dynamax a Pokémon, press [button-icon-1] when you see the red Dynamax symbol appear. If you choose to Dynamax your Pokémon, the effect will last for three turns. During this time period, each of your Pokémon’s moves will be powered up into special variants known as [color-green-2]Max Moves[color-red-3]. These Max Moves are much more powerful than regular attacks, so make sure you use them to full effect while Dynamaxed!

source.original:
"Do you know about the
Hall of Fame?

It’s the place where you go if you
defeat the Pokémon League!

At one point, the old Champion,
Artie had been there so many times,\lhe decided to set a goal of going\lthere with every team consisting\lof a common type.

Sadly, he never did reach his goal,
and only ever entered with monotype\lteams for 17 out of the 18 types.

Maybe you want to take up the
challenge instead?"

At one point, the old Champion, Artie had been there so many times, he decided to set a goal of going there with every team consisting of a common type. Sadly, he never did reach his goal, and only ever entered with monotype teams for 17 out of the 18 types. Maybe you want to take up the challenge instead?

source.original:
"You’re taking up the challenge?
Sweet!

Bring on those victories!

There are [green]18[blue] types in total, and
you’ll need to enter the Hall of\lFame with teams for each one.

Oh, and keep this in mind: if you
Mega Evolve a Pokémon, both the\lbase species and Mega species will\lcount towards the team type.

So, let’s say you want to use a
Mega Gyarados.

In addition to a Water-type team,
you could use it on both Flying-\land Dark-type teams!"
source.translation_source: You’re taking up the challenge? Sweet! Bring on those victories! There are [color-green-1]18[color-blue-2] types in total, and you’ll need to enter the Hall of Fame with teams for each one. Oh, and keep this in mind: if you Mega Evolve a Pokémon, both the base species and Mega species will count towards the team type. So, let’s say you want to use a Mega Gyarados. In addition to a Water-type team, you could use it on both Flying- and Dark-type teams!

choose to quit, the game is over."

source.original:

spots to start diggin’."

source.original:
"Trainer Tips!

Pokémon can gain Exp. Points by
battling other Pokémon.

Exp. Points help them grow
stronger.

And your Pokémon will still get
Exp. Points even if you catch a\lPokémon you are battling against!

But keep in mind, if your Pokémon
level up too much, other Trainers\lwill get stronger as well.

In order to prevent issues from
arising due to overleveling such\las increased difficulty, a hard\llevel cap may be enabled from the\l[green]Options Menu[black] by setting [green]Exp. Gain[black]\lto [green]Capped Exp. Share[black]."

Points even if you catch a Pokémon you are battling against! But keep in mind, if your Pokémon level up too much, other Trainers will get stronger as well. In order to prevent issues from arising due to overleveling such as increased difficulty, a hard level cap may be enabled from the [color-green-1]Options Menu[color-black-2] by setting [color-green-3]Exp. Gain[color-black-4] to [color-green-5]Capped Exp. Share[color-black-6].

source.original:
"Trainer Tips!

When selecting an attack in battle,
certain symbols may appear.

This is based on the move’s
effectiveness against the target.

A green [green]\au[black] indicates that the move
is super effective.

A yellow [orange]\ad[black] indicates the move is
not very effective.

A red [lightgreen]*[black] indicates that the move
doesn’t affect the target at all.

And a \+ symbol indicates the move
has the Same-Type-Attack-Bonus."

A green [color-green-1][game-token-2][color-black-3] indicates that the move is super effective. A yellow [color-orange-4][game-token-5][color-black-6] indicates the move is not very effective. A red [color-lightgreen-7]*[color-black-8] indicates that the move doesn’t affect the target at all. And a [game-token-9] symbol indicates the move has the Same-Type-Attack-Bonus.

source.original:
"Trainer Tips!

The [green]Item Restrictions[black] option lets
you choose how many items you can\luse in battle!

If you choose [green]No Items[black], then no
Trainers will be able to use any\leither!

At minimum, [green]4 Items Only[black] must be
set for [green]Expert[black], and [green]No Items[black] must\lbe set for [green]Insane[black].

If you’re feeling extra ambitious,
setting it to [green]Enemy Trainer Only[black]\lwill allow your opponents to use\litems while preventing you!

This last choice works for any
difficulty."

If you choose [color-green-3]No Items[color-black-4], then no Trainers will be able to use any either! At minimum, [color-green-5]4 Items Only[color-black-6] must be set for [color-green-7]Expert[color-black-8], and [color-green-9]No Items[color-black-10] must be set for [color-green-11]Insane[color-black-12]. If you’re feeling extra ambitious, setting it to [color-green-13]Enemy Trainer Only[color-black-14] will allow your opponents to use items while preventing you! This last choice works for any difficulty.

source.original:
"Trainer Tips!

Avoid using standard Balls such as
Ultra Balls when attempting to\lcapture powerful Pokémon!

If you’re facing a very [green]heavy[black]
Pokémon, the [green]Heavy Ball[black] will be\lthe ideal Ball.

Otherwise if the battle has been
drawn out for over [green]10 turns[black],\lconsider using a [green]Timer Ball[black].

If the battle has been short, but
the opposing Pokémon has a [green]base\lSpeed stat[black] over [green]100[black], then consider\lusing a [green]Fast Ball[black].

But if the battle has been short and
the opposing Pokémon is slow, then\lattempt to catch the Pokémon at\l[green]night[black] using a [green]Dusk Ball[black].

These four Balls will be key in
capturing powerful Pokémon quickly!"
source.translation_source: Trainer Tips! Avoid using standard Balls such as Ultra Balls when attempting to capture powerful Pokémon! If you’re facing a very [color-green-1]heavy[color-black-2] Pokémon, the [color-green-3]Heavy Ball[color-black-4] will be the ideal Ball. Otherwise if the battle has been drawn out for over [color-green-5]10 turns[color-black-6], consider using a [color-green-7]Timer Ball[color-black-8]. If the battle has been short, but the opposing Pokémon has a [color-green-9]base Speed stat[color-black-10] over [color-green-11]100[color-black-12], then consider using a [color-green-13]Fast Ball[color-black-14]. But if the battle has been short and the opposing Pokémon is slow, then attempt to catch the Pokémon at [color-green-15]night[color-black-16] using a [color-green-17]Dusk Ball[color-black-18]. These four Balls will be key in capturing powerful Pokémon quickly!

entries.content_family_evidence: Extractor category/table ownership or PROVEN direct speaker binding; UNKNOWN otherwise.

source.original:
"Hello there, Trainer.

Maxima.

If you’re here, then I should
congratulate you for navigating\lyour way to me.

I presume, like many others, you
have come here seeking the power\lof [green]Mega Evolution[red]?

\.

As I thought.

However, it is one thing to \qowant\qc.
It is quite another to \qodeserve\qc.

You see, Mega Evolution is only
possible when both Trainer and\lPokémon share a deep bond.

Yet, there are those who visit me,
focused only on what perceived\lpower can be achieved with\lMega Evolution.

And the bonds that make Mega
Evolution possible\.\CC0818 are not always\lbonds of friendship and love.

So, if I am to pass on such a
technique to someone, it must be\lsomeone of both skill, and a\lnatural love for Pokémon.

This shall be my final test."

source.original:
"I see.

[buffer1] very well, myself.

[green]Mega Evolve[red] your Pokémon.

Mega Evolving in battle, it must\lbe holding its unique [green]Mega Stone[red].

Mega Evolve by the [green]Mega Symbol[red] in\lthe battle menu.

Should it appear, press \btn04
before you select your next\lattack.

Your Pokémon will then Mega Evolve
and become more powerful.

Keep in mind, however, you can
only Mega Evolve a Pokémon [green]once[red]\lper battle, and it wears off if the\lbattle ends, or the Mega Evolved\lPokémon faints.

Now, take that power\.\CC0818 and use it
for the good of humanity.

I shall be counting on you to change
the world\.\CC0818 and make a real impact\."
source.translation_source: I see. Yes, I think you do carry that [buffer1-1] very well, myself. Anyway, you now have the power to [color-green-2]Mega Evolve[color-red-3] your Pokémon. For a Pokémon to be capable of Mega Evolving in battle, it must be holding its unique [color-green-4]Mega Stone[color-red-5]. You should see if that Pokémon can Mega Evolve by the [color-green-6]Mega Symbol[color-red-7] in the battle menu. Should it appear, press [button-icon-8] before you select your next attack. you to the other side.

You won’t even have to get your
feet wet.

What do you say?
It’s only a measly $[green]200000[blue]\."

source.original:
"The Battle Circus is a facility for
Single, Double, and Multi Battle\lchallenges.

Once begun, your challenge lasts
until you defeat the Circus\lRingmaster, or you choose to rest.

In Single Battle format, you have a
choice of entering with three or\lsix Pokémon.

In Double Battle format, you have a
choice of entering with four or six\lPokémon.

The battles are held in the main
arena.

Before each battle, the Ringmaster
will activate a random effect for\lthe duration of the battle.

This effect is permanent and cannot
be removed or overridden.

These effects may also increase in
intensity and begin to stack the\lhigher your streak becomes.

For every Trainer you defeat, you
will earn [green]Battle Points[blue] ([green]BP[blue]).

If you want to interrupt your
challenge, your progress will be\lrecorded for when you wish to\lcontinue.

If at any point you leave without
saving, you will be disqualified\lfrom your challenge.

Please be aware of that!"
source.translation_source: The Battle Circus is a facility for Single, Double, and Multi Battle challenges. Once begun, your challenge lasts until you defeat the Circus Ringmaster, or you choose to rest. In Single Battle format, you have a choice of entering with three or six Pokémon. In Double Battle format, you have a choice of entering with four or six Pokémon. The battles are held in the main arena. Before each battle, the Ringmaster will activate a random effect for the duration of the battle. This effect is permanent and cannot be removed or overridden. These effects may also increase in intensity and begin to stack the higher your streak becomes. For every Trainer you defeat, you will earn [color-green-1]Battle Points[color-blue-2] ([color-green-3]BP[color-blue-4]). If you want to interrupt your challenge, your progress will be recorded for when you wish to continue. If at any point you leave without saving, you will be disqualified from your challenge. Please be aware of that!

source.original:
"The Battle Circus is a facility for
Single, Double, and Multi Battle\lchallenges.

Once begun, your challenge lasts
until you defeat the Circus\lRingmaster, or you choose to rest.

The Battle Circus’ Multi Battle
show is for Multi Battles with a\lpartner.

To enter, join another Trainer and
compete with two or three Pokémon\leach.

Underneath the circus is a room
named the Battle Salon where you\lcan meet other Trainers.

There you can find a Trainer to act
as your partner in the Multi\lBattles.

You can also partner up with a
friend using a Link Cable.

Once you have partnered up, you
will be shown to the main arena.

In the arena, tag teams will
challenge you.

Before each battle, the Ringmaster
will activate a random effect for\lthe duration of the battle.

This effect is permanent and cannot
be removed or overridden.

These effects may also increase in
intensity and begin to stack the\lhigher your streak becomes.

If you manage to defeat each team,
you will earn Battle Points (BP).

If you want to interrupt your
challenge, your progress will be\lrecorded for when you wish to\lcontinue.

If at any point you leave without
saving, you will be disqualified\lfrom your challenge.

Also, if you are in a tag team with
a friend, you may not interrupt\lyour challenge.

Please be aware of that!"
source.translation_source: The Battle Circus is a facility for Single, Double, and Multi Battle challenges. Once begun, your challenge lasts until you defeat the Circus Ringmaster, or you choose to rest. The Battle Circus’ Multi Battle show is for Multi Battles with a partner. To enter, join another Trainer and compete with two or three Pokémon each. Underneath the circus is a room named the Battle Salon where you can meet other Trainers. There you can find a Trainer to act as your partner in the Multi Battles. You can also partner up with a friend using a Link Cable. Once you have partnered up, you will be shown to the main arena. In the arena, tag teams will challenge you. Before each battle, the Ringmaster will activate a random effect for the duration of the battle. This effect is permanent and cannot be removed or overridden. These effects may also increase in intensity and begin to stack the higher your streak becomes. If you manage to defeat each team, you will earn Battle Points (BP). If you want to interrupt your challenge, your progress will be recorded for when you wish to continue. If at any point you leave without saving, you will be disqualified from your challenge. Also, if you are in a tag team with a friend, you may not interrupt your challenge. Please be aware of that!

"Ladies and gentlemen, boys and

show, but I, Ringmaster Paula\.

ring, to test our latest star!

terms of tactics, and adaptation\.

understand what it is our audience\ltruly came to see?

source.original:
"The Battle Mine is a facility for
special challenges.

Once begun, your challenge lasts
until you defeat the Mine\lExcavator, or you choose to rest.

On each level you descend in the
mine, a Trainer awaits you.

The format you choose determines
which tier they can be battled in,\land your depth determines other\lbattle settings, such as Single or\lDouble, level, party size, Inverse\lBattles, and Dynamax.

For a list of tiers, please see my
\qo[green]Battle Tiers[blue]\qc section.

For every Trainer you defeat, you
will earn [green]Battle Points[blue] ([green]BP[blue]).

Additionally, upon defeat, some
Trainers may drop the items they\lwere mining, for you to collect.

If you want to interrupt your
challenge, your progress will be\lrecorded for when you wish to\lcontinue.

If at any point you leave without
saving, you will be disqualified\lfrom your challenge.

Please be aware of that!"
source.translation_source: The Battle Mine is a facility for special challenges. Once begun, your challenge lasts until you defeat the Mine Excavator, or you choose to rest. On each level you descend in the mine, a Trainer awaits you. The format you choose determines which tier they can be battled in, and your depth determines other battle settings, such as Single or Double, level, party size, Inverse Battles, and Dynamax. For a list of tiers, please see my [quote-open-1][color-green-2]Battle Tiers[color-blue-3][quote-close-4] section. For every Trainer you defeat, you will earn [color-green-5]Battle Points[color-blue-6] ([color-green-7]BP[color-blue-8]). Additionally, upon defeat, some Trainers may drop the items they were mining, for you to collect. If you want to interrupt your challenge, your progress will be recorded for when you wish to continue. If at any point you leave without saving, you will be disqualified from your challenge. Please be aware of that!

source.original:
"The Battle Sands is a facility for
Single and Double Battles.

In Single Battles, two Pokémon
must be entered.

In Double Battles, three Pokémon
must be entered.

Here’s the catch for this facility:
you’re not actually battling.

Pokémon you enter in this facility
will be taken by a volunteer and\lused to fight for you.

You’ll be given the choice of
whether you want your Pokémon to\lattack or switch out, but the final\ldecision will be up to the Trainer\lcontrolling your Pokémon.

As this Trainer wins battles,
[green]Battle Points[blue] ([green]BP[blue]) will be acrued.

You may choose to stop the battles
at any point, but know that once\lyou do, that’s it for the streak.

Whether the Trainer loses a battle
or you decide to retire, you will\lreceive the BP acrued as winnings.

Additionally, leaving at any point
without saving will cause any BP\lacrued to be lost.

Just be aware of that.

Oh, I forgot to mention that one
Pokémon on each side of the field\lwill gain a random stat boost at\lthe beginning of the battle.

Keep that in mind when choosing
your Pokémon."
source.translation_source: The Battle Sands is a facility for Single and Double Battles. In Single Battles, two Pokémon must be entered. In Double Battles, three Pokémon must be entered. Here’s the catch for this facility: you’re not actually battling. Pokémon you enter in this facility will be taken by a volunteer and used to fight for you. You’ll be given the choice of whether you want your Pokémon to attack or switch out, but the final decision will be up to the Trainer controlling your Pokémon. As this Trainer wins battles, [color-green-1]Battle Points[color-blue-2] ([color-green-3]BP[color-blue-4]) will be acrued. You may choose to stop the battles at any point, but know that once you do, that’s it for the streak. Whether the Trainer loses a battle or you decide to retire, you will receive the BP acrued as winnings. Additionally, leaving at any point without saving will cause any BP acrued to be lost. Just be aware of that. Oh, I forgot to mention that one Pokémon on each side of the field will gain a random stat boost at the beginning of the battle. Keep that in mind when choosing your Pokémon.

source.original:
"The Battle Tower is a facility for
Single, Double, Multi, and\lMetronome Battle challenges.

Once begun, your challenge lasts
until you defeat the Tower Tycoon,\lor you choose to rest.

In Single Battle format, you have a
choice of entering with three or\lsix Pokémon.

In Double Battle format, you have a
choice of entering with four or\lsix Pokémon.

The battles are held in Battle
Rooms of which there are many in\lthe tower.

In each of the Battle Rooms,
Trainers await your challenge.

For every Trainer you defeat, you
will earn [green]Battle Points[blue] ([green]BP[blue]).

If you want to interrupt your
challenge, your progress will be\lrecorded for when you wish to\lcontinue.

If at any point you leave without
saving, you will be disqualified\lfrom your challenge.

Please be aware of that!"
source.translation_source: The Battle Tower is a facility for Single, Double, Multi, and Metronome Battle challenges. Once begun, your challenge lasts until you defeat the Tower Tycoon, or you choose to rest. In Single Battle format, you have a choice of entering with three or six Pokémon. In Double Battle format, you have a choice of entering with four or six Pokémon. The battles are held in Battle Rooms of which there are many in the tower. In each of the Battle Rooms, Trainers await your challenge. For every Trainer you defeat, you will earn [color-green-1]Battle Points[color-blue-2] ([color-green-3]BP[color-blue-4]). If you want to interrupt your challenge, your progress will be recorded for when you wish to continue. If at any point you leave without saving, you will be disqualified from your challenge. Please be aware of that!

source.original:
"[green]Dynamax[black] is a temporary
transformation where a Pokémon\ldistorts space to change its size.

When a Pokémon Dynamaxes, for
three turns its HP is increased and\lall of its moves are powered up\linto special [green]Max Moves[black].

Each Max Move has a unique effect,
that varies based on the type of\lthe original move.

If a Pokémon has the Gigantamax
Factor, it can undergo Gigantamax.

This is a special kind of Dynamax
that results in a different\lappearance to its regular form, in\laddition to being larger.

Each Gigantamax Pokémon has an
exclusive Max Move known as a\lG-Max Move.

To activate Dynamax, press
\btn04 while selecting an attack\lto use."
source.translation_source: [color-green-1]Dynamax[color-black-2] is a temporary transformation where a Pokémon distorts space to change its size. When a Pokémon Dynamaxes, for three turns its HP is increased and all of its moves are powered up into special [color-green-3]Max Moves[color-black-4]. Each Max Move has a unique effect, that varies based on the type of the original move. If a Pokémon has the Gigantamax Factor, it can undergo Gigantamax. facility only for Single Battle\lchallenges.

until you choose to rest.

Regigigas with the Ability Stall in
addition to Pokémon banned in the\l[green]Standard[blue] tier may not be used."

source.original:
"Before each battle, your opponent’s
team will be revealed to you.

Additionally, in each battle, a
certain move type may not be used.

This will be revealed as well.

Regarding moves that change types,
the type they change into is taken\linto account.

It is at that point you must choose
a single Pokémon to fight against\lone of theirs.

For every Trainer you defeat, you
will earn [green]Battle Points[blue] ([green]BP[blue]).

However, do note that since this
battle facility is not part of the\lBattle Frontier, you will not earn\lany prints for your Frontier Card.

If you want to interrupt your
challenge, your progress will be\lrecorded for when you wish to\lcontinue.

If at any point you leave without
saving, you will be disqualified\lfrom your challenge.

Please be aware of that!"
source.translation_source: Before each battle, your opponent’s team will be revealed to you. Additionally, in each battle, a certain move type may not be used. This will be revealed as well. Regarding moves that change types, the type they change into is taken into account. It is at that point you must choose a single Pokémon to fight against one of theirs. For every Trainer you defeat, you will earn [color-green-1]Battle Points[color-blue-2] ([color-green-3]BP[color-blue-4]). However, do note that since this battle facility is not part of the Battle Frontier, you will not earn any prints for your Frontier Card. If you want to interrupt your challenge, your progress will be recorded for when you wish to continue. If at any point you leave without saving, you will be disqualified from your challenge. Please be aware of that!

"[black]Dynamax is a unique phenomenon that

your Pokémon’s moves will be\lpowered up into special variants\lknown as [green]Max Moves[black].

These Max Moves are much more
powerful than regular attacks."
